I'm a software engineer focused on AI enablement and modernization: moving legacy code, stacks, and workflows onto modern ones, with AI doing the heavy lifting and a person checking the work. I care most about the checking. Anyone can generate a migration; the value is in catching the wrong measurement, the missed dependency, and the claim that doesn't hold up. Below is work I can show, plus what I learned doing it.

Projects

  1. Legacy App Migration to a New Stack, Built with AI

    Migrated a legacy photo-gallery app to Angular, ASP.NET Core, Azure Cosmos DB, and Blob Storage, a stack I hadn't used before, with Claude as a working partner. I made the design decisions and verified every claim myself. Response compression alone cut CSS from 232 KB to 49 KB over the wire, and a fresh clone runs in 16 seconds with 13 commands. The README states what was and wasn't measured.

    Angular · ASP.NET Core · Azure Cosmos DB | Live Source

  2. Agentic Removal of a Deprecated Feature

    Removed a deprecated, still-live feature from a production codebase using a multi-pass agentic workflow: map dependencies, verify, escalate scope questions, then execute. The initial scope undercounted the real dependency graph, and the workflow surfaced multiple corrections instead of guessing. Result: 300+ files removed in about half a day across a stack of CI-passing pull requests.

    Agentic Workflows · CI/CD · Code Migration

  3. AI Agent Skill for Design-System Migration

    Built a custom AI agent skill, using spec-driven development, to run a design-system migration end to end per library: branch creation, automated code migration, generated verification guides, and quality gates. Per-library effort dropped from hours of manual work to near-zero, covering two dozen libraries in about three weeks.

    Spec-Driven Development · AI Agent Skills · Code Migration
